1.title: Disaster Recovery and High Availability
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Disaster Recovery and High Availability. It covers the exam area three point zero Network Operations. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. three point three Explain disaster recovery (D R) concepts: D R metrics (R P O, R T O, M T T R, M T B F). D R sites (cold, warm, hot). High-availability approaches (active-active, active-passive). Testing (tabletop exercises, validation tests). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: three point zero Network Operations (nineteen percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: DR metrics
1.text: D R metrics. The figure shows this: A timeline showing the last backup, the disaster, and the R P O and R T O intervals.

1.title: DR metrics, continued
1.text: D R metrics. R P O (recovery point objective). How much data loss is acceptable, measured in time before the disaster (R P O of four hours equals backups at least every four hours). R T O (recovery time objective). How long the service may be down before it must be restored. M T T R (mean time to repair). Average time to fix a failed component. M T B F (mean time between failures). Average time a component runs before it fails (reliability). Exam tip: R P O looks backward (data lost). R T O looks forward (time to recover). M T T R is repair time; M T B F is time between failures.

1.title: DR sites
1.text: D R sites. Cold site. State: Space and power only; no equipment or data. Recovery time: Longest (days to weeks). Cost: Lowest. Warm site. State: Equipment installed, data not current (restore from backup). Recovery time: Hours to days. Cost: Medium. Hot site. State: Fully equipped and running with near real-time data. Recovery time: Minutes or seconds. Cost: Highest.

1.title: High availability
1.text: High availability. Active-active. All nodes serve traffic at once; load shared; if one fails, the others absorb its load. Active-passive. One node serves; a standby waits and takes over on failure (failover). H A reduces single points of failure: redundant power, links, devices (F H R P, link aggregation, clusters).

1.title: Testing
1.text: Testing. Tabletop exercise. Staff talk through a disaster scenario step by step, no systems touched. Validation test. Actually restore or fail over to prove the plan works. Exam tip: "Walk through the plan in a meeting" equals tabletop exercise. "Prove the backups restore" equals validation test. Exam tip: Cold less than warm less than hot for cost and speed. A hot site is running with current data.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company can accept losing at most two hours of data. Which metric states this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: An R P O of two hours. R P O is the acceptable amount of data loss measured in time.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A service must be restored within thirty minutes of an outage. Which metric states this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: An R T O of thirty minutes. R T O is the maximum acceptable downtime.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A company wants a recovery site with equipment ready and near real-time data for the fastest recovery. Which site fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A hot site. Hot sites are fully equipped and current.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which site type provides only space and power with no equipment installed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A cold site. Cold sites are empty shells.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Two firewalls both pass traffic and share the load, and one absorbs everything if the other fails. Which approach is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Active-active. In active-active all nodes serve traffic.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Management wants staff to discuss a ransomware scenario around a table without touching systems. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A tabletop exercise. Tabletop exercises are discussion-based.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does R P O measure? Answer: Acceptable data loss, in time. Question two. What does M T B F measure? Answer: Average time between failures. Question three. Which D R site is the cheapest? Answer: A cold site.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What happens in active-passive? Answer: A standby node takes over when the active node fails. Question five. What is a validation test? Answer: Actually restoring or failing over to prove the plan works. Question six. What does M T T R measure? Answer: Average time to repair a failed component.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Metrics: R P O (data loss), R T O (downtime), M T T R (repair), M T B F (between failures). Sites: cold (shell), warm (equipment, old data), hot (running, current). H A: active-active (shared), active-passive (standby). Testing: tabletop (discussion), validation (real restore).
